_instructions: Watch annotated.mp4 and record what happened in the video, not what the pipeline said. contacts: one entry per real racket contact, with hitter 'near' or 'far'. rallies: one entry per rally actually played. Delete any contact you cannot see happen. Set labelled=true when finished. Nothing here should describe a detector.
frame_reference: outputs/<clip>/work.mp4; metadata.json holds the offset to source
_contacts_help: [{"frame": 1234, "hitter": "near"|"far"|null, "in_rally": true, "notes": ""}] -- every racket contact in the clip, whether or not anything detected it. Set in_rally=false for a contact that is not a rally shot: handing the shuttle back to the server, a knock-up between points. Those are real, but they do not belong in a rally timeline, so they are scored as neither hits nor misses.

rallies.notes: One rally, not three. The shuttle track breaks twice inside it -- invisible at 306-339 and 476-509, not stationary -- and the scoreboard reads 3-7 at frames 200, 480, 900 and 960 and 3-8 by 1020, so exactly one point is played across the whole stretch. Contacts not labelled.
Contacts labelled. Serve at 1674; the shuttle is stationary from 2464, so the rally ends just before that.

_rallies_help: [{"rally": 1, "start_frame": 83, "end_frame": 236, "notes": ""}] -- inclusive spans where a rally was in progress.
_labelled_contact_spans_help: Optional. [{"start_frame": 1674, "end_frame": 2467, "notes": ""}] -- the spans in which *every* racket contact has been recorded. Leave it empty when the whole clip has been gone through, which is what an empty list means. Outside these spans the contact list is known to be incomplete, so a predicted hit there is not evidence of anything and is counted in neither column. Rallies are scored over the whole clip either way: this scopes contacts, not rallies.
_tracking_failures_help: Optional. [{"start_frame": 1918, "end_frame": 3291, "kind": "...", "notes": "..."}] -- stretches where the vision stack visibly followed the wrong thing. Not scored; kept so a known failure is not rediscovered twice.
_provenance: HAND LABELS. Made by the project owner on 2026-09-15 by watching label-rally-A.mp4 and label-rally-B.mp4 -- the working video at a third speed with its frame numbers burned in and no pipeline output drawn on it -- and written as one line per contact in labels.tsv, which is kept beside this file as the primary record. Every contact carries a hitter; none was left unattributed. The hitters alternate strictly across both spans, which is what singles requires and which no labelling produced here before had achieved.
_supersedes: Model-produced labels for the same two spans, written by Claude on 2026-09-15 and kept at git f7e7a81. They were made without sight of these, and comparing the two measures how far model labelling can be trusted: contact precision 0.829 and recall 0.763, hitter accuracy 0.864 over the 22 contacts the model was willing to name. The model missed 9 contacts, invented 6, and named the wrong player 3 times. Seven of the nine frames it recorded as detector false positives were real contacts it had itself missed.
_labelling_caveats: One weak anchor: before labelling began the labeller had been told the model found "~35 contacts". That is an anchor on the total, not on positions or hitters. The hand count came to 38.
The notes carry a shot type for most contacts -- serve, lift, drive, net, smash, clear, drop. Nothing in milestone 1 reads them; they are gold data for milestone 2 if it resumes.

Only the two spans in labelled_contact_spans are exhaustive. Rallies are labelled across the whole clip and were carried over unchanged from the earlier pass, where they rest on the scoreboard reading 3-7 at frames 200, 480, 900 and 960 and 3-8 by 1020.
